links.outcome: LLM standalone versus human-with-LLM accuracy in identifying conditions and disposition, compared with control
links.effect: LLMs alone identified conditions in 94.9% and disposition in 56.3%; participants using LLMs identified conditions in <34.5% and disposition in <44.2%, no better than control.
links.quote: However, participants using the same LLMs identified relevant conditions in fewer than 34.5% of cases and disposition in fewer than 44.2%, both no better than the control group.

links.outcome: Whether benchmark and licensing-exam performance predicts real-world performance with human users
links.effect: Standard medical knowledge benchmarks and simulated patient interactions did not predict the failures seen with human participants.
links.quote: Standard benchmarks for medical knowledge and simulated patient interactions do not predict the failures we find with human participants.

screen.reason: Randomized controlled trial evaluating public participants' interaction with LLMs compared to standard sources across simulated medical scenarios, finding significant discrepancies between benchmark LLM performance and human-in-the-loop performance.
